summary.notes: 19 reviewer-labelled cases, 1 excluded as ambiguous. Labels recorded before scoring; assessor output not shown during labelling. Refusals counted as wrong in accuracy. Synthetic cases are author-constructed and are reported separately from real-evidence cases, never pooled.

rows.reviewer_reason: confirm human oversight policy include details over a human decides rather than just reviews. what information the human receives, and what authority they hold to override. oversight metrics, rollback plans. overrides were recorded with reason.

inspect register that should include the resources an AI system depends on - data, tooling, computing and human resoruces. the register requires to capture this dependencies and not only a list of models. confirm each entry carries an owner, materiality, lifecycle status.

established validation standard. confirm the scope is defined, independence is defined structurally. organisation run security review across its own AI-generated code and pipelines. validator sits outside the developing function. confirm a validation outcome exists for the version deployed. deployment approval with limitations and residual risk stated. evidence of stress testing like red-team.

AI use policy. confirm scope covers the AI in the inventory. the pririncipals are stated as requirements with owners. confirm four FEAT principles map onto F1-F4 as their implementing controls. confirm review cycle met. and that exceptions were approved at the authority the policy reserves them to.

detailed use cases in the inventory and test coverage: for each, confirm the MGF D1-D4 and SAFR S1-S4 controls are in scope and have assessment status. test concentration and trace how many in-scope use cases depend on a single foundation model provider. exposure needs to be reported and require a decisionon taken.

inspect the materiality methodology confirm impact, complexity and reliance are defined with criteria a second assessor could apply to the same case and reach the same tier. named materiality scores and rationales. confirm each names an assessor and date, that the tier follows arithmentically from the recoorded scores. a tier no second assessor can reproduce from the recorded rationale is the near miss

need the training plan, confirm documentation of roles (board, model owners, first line users, control functions). the completion is mandated with a consequence. thus addresses AI literaccy and not only policy awareness.  confirm non-completion was followed up. and training content refreshed after material regulatory changes

documented terms of reference. confirm members from various dept (risk, technology, business, compliance, legal) holds decision rights rather advisory standing. the committee is the decision maker. reconcile minutes against those step outputs to test whether it decided what the play say it decides
capacity and performance plan. review plan against actual consumption, constraints were escalated. monitoring and logging tooling is provisioned.

establish monitoring standards. confirm any drift, performance and stability metrics are defined with threshold and an owner, that alerting routes to someone who can act. the revalidation and backtesting cadence is set by materiality. reconstruct evidence of monitoring dashboards. continuous monitor of threshold breaches produced a recorded response, and that supporessed or muted alerts were reviewed.
training plan, confirm roles and users. test completion for mandateded population, follow up on non-completion
